findings.heading: Troubleshooting common errors
findings.proposition: Setting RStudio to always run as administrator is advantageous when working from an Rproject, because you then open the project file rather than clicking the RStudio icon.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader is told to right-click the icon but is never told WHY a permanent administrator setting is needed. An Rproject user, who never clicks the RStudio icon, will right-click once, get an elevated session that day, and not understand why the C: library option disappears again the next time they open the project from the .Rproj file.

findings.heading: Troubleshooting common errors
findings.proposition: The instructions for installing TinyTex are on the R basics page, linked at basics.qmd.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish text writes the reference as a bare bracketed label with no link target, so it renders as literal text '[R temelleri]' rather than a hyperlink. A reader who needs the TinyTex installation instructions has no way to reach the page from here and must search the handbook manually.

findings.heading: Troubleshooting common errors
findings.proposition: The literal R error text is 'Error in tools::startDynamicHelp() : internet routines cannot be loaded'.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish version renders the quoted error literal as 'internet rutinleri yuklenemiyor', a string R never emits. A reader matching the message in their console against the handbook, or pasting it into a search engine to find the same fix, will not match this section.
